key_insight: Residual learning with convex projection improves quantum error mitigation while ensuring reconstructed density matrices remain physically valid.
engineering_relevance: The framework can improve noisy-hardware bound-state simulations, but training-state selection and regression-model choice affect accuracy.
method: Learn error corrections using residual regression, then apply convex projection to enforce density-matrix validity.
Evaluate Haar-random versus VQE-ansatz training states and different regression models.
Compare with conventional ML-QEM, readout error mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation.
evidence_signal: On IBM hardware, three-qubit Λ-deuteron simulations achieved −0.134 MeV versus an ideal −0.135 MeV with 0.999 fidelity; four-qubit Λ–α simulations achieved −3.014 and −3.045 MeV with fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998.
watch_item: Results cover only three- and four-qubit systems; scalability and generalization beyond the evaluated training distributions remain unestablished.
paper_title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
